title: Cards

payload.content: Primary and supplementary cards share a governed relationship, but supplementary issuance and servicing require validated primary-cardholder authority, product eligibility and clear linked-card impact.

Commercial cards require an eligible organizational relationship, authorized requester, configured employee/procurement/travel/expense controls and generic credit or funding treatment without inventing bank-specific policy.

businessRules.rule: Only card products available for the customer, channel, relationship and applicable jurisdiction may be selected.
Customer identity, relationship status and required consent must be resolved before application submission.
The selected card family and form determine applicable funding, credit, fulfilment, servicing and billing behavior.
A linked funding account must be eligible, owned or validly entitled, active and usable for a debit-card relationship.
Credit-card issuance requires an eligible credit facility or approved credit-account relationship.
Supplementary-card issuance requires an eligible primary relationship and authorized primary-cardholder context.
Commercial-card issuance requires an eligible organizational relationship and authorized requester.
An application must contain all mandatory product, customer, account, credit, consent and fulfilment information before approval.
Approval must be performed by an authorized role whenever the product, credit or risk configuration requires approval.
Duplicate or uncertain issuance requests must be reconciled before a new card account or card record is created.
Physical-card fulfilment and virtual-card provisioning must follow separate applicable routes.
Activation requires an issued card, eligible status, successful customer verification and confirmed receipt or secure provisioning.
PIN and security credentials must never be exposed in business content, logs, notifications or unauthorized channels.
Only card statuses permitted for the requested transaction or servicing action may proceed.
Expired, closed, lost, stolen or compromised cards must not authorize new transactions except controlled exceptions expressly supported by policy.
Transactions must respect enabled POS, e-commerce, contactless, ATM, recurring, international and tokenized-usage controls.
Transactions must comply with applicable card, account, product, channel, merchant, geography, currency and velocity limits.
Debit and prepaid authorization must evaluate available balance; credit authorization must evaluate available credit.
Authentication and step-up requirements depend on transaction context and applicable security policy.
The authorization response must reflect the authoritative fraud and risk decision, including approve, decline, authentication-required, hold, referral or unavailable.
Authorization holds must be created, adjusted, released, expired or reversed consistently with clearing and product rules.
Potential duplicate authorizations, clearing records and postings must be detected before financial duplication occurs.
Clearing, posting and settlement mismatches must be reconciled before final completion is asserted.
Credit billing, minimum payment, due date, allocation, interest, fees and delinquency treatment apply according to applicable product configuration and bank policy.
Credit-card payments must be allocated and posted consistently before available credit and statement status are updated.
Cash advances and over-limit outcomes require explicit product eligibility and applicable credit controls.
Temporary lock, channel-control and limit changes require authenticated authorization and auditable state synchronization.
Replacement and renewal require eligible status, controlled old-card transition and activation of the new card.
Closure requires resolution of outstanding obligations, pending transactions, disputes and linked supplementary cards.
Dispute and chargeback handling must validate eligibility, evidence and applicable timeframes without fabricating scheme-specific deadlines.
Retry after an uncertain technical outcome is permitted only after reconciliation establishes whether the original action succeeded.
Every material decision, override, retry, financial adjustment and manual action must retain audit evidence.

successOutcome.description: The card reaches an authorized ACTIVE state and is subsequently serviced, replaced, renewed or closed through controlled, auditable outcomes.
